solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fancy a ringer took the lead

indicators.note: the ringer went in front, so the ringer's letters come before the single letter

parts.note: a chimer is one who rings bells, a bell-ringer

explanation.surface: A substitute player or horse moved ahead of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringer' suggests a lookalike substitute, but here it is someone who rings bells; 'took the lead' puts CHIMER in front of A.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a wild fancy or illusory imagining, a product of the imagination.

clue.text: Agreement on tailless aircraft

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is removed from the aircraft's name

parts.note: Concorde was the supersonic airliner

explanation.surface: A deal is struck over a plane without its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Concord means harmony or accord between parties, an agreement.

clue.text: Medal-winners like ABC?

definitions.meaning: gold, silver and bronze go to those finishing top three
A, B and C open the alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: Medal-winners finish in the top three places, just as A, B and C are the alphabet's opening letters.

clue.text: Case quite confusing, not initially

indicators.note: confusing says the remaining letters are jumbled into a new order
not initially means the opening letter of the word quite is dropped

explanation.surface: A legal matter is proving rather puzzling, apart from its start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' drops Q from QUITE to leave UITE, which 'confusing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles or toiletries.

clue.text: Has made trouble when embarrassed

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters are stirred up into another order

explanation.surface: Someone has caused trouble and now feels awkward about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashamed means feeling embarrassment or guilt over something done.

clue.text: Tremulous gleam covers him, mercifully only partly

indicators.note: only partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is kindly given only partial cover, as if by a blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: A shimmer is a soft wavering light, exactly a tremulous gleam.

clue.text: Prop certain to sound more costly

indicators.note: to sound means the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: sure means certain
when prices are up, things are more costly

explanation.surface: A stage prop is sure to sound pricier than it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prop' looks like a noun but is the verb: to support.
explanation.definitionFit: To shore up is to prop up with supports, as with a wall.

clue.text: Metal press

definitions.meaning: a common magnetic metallic element, Fe
to smooth clothes with a heated appliance

explanation.definitionFit: Iron is the metallic element, and to iron clothes is to press them.

clue.text: Have a brush with success?

parts.note: a brush can sweep, so a broom's thorough work stands for winning everything

explanation.definitionFit: To win every prize or contest is idiomatically to clear the board entirely with a broom's work.

clue.text: Hotel that is right to be more luxuriously elegant

parts.note: the Ritz is a famous luxury hotel in London
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A posh hotel is the right place to be more stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritzy means luxuriously smart, so the comparative means more so.

clue.text: Little scenery and it's fairly unattractive

definitions.meaning: literally, scarcely any view worth seeing
the idiom used of a plain-looking person or thing

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for something plain, and read literally it means there is hardly anything to view.

clue.text: Steers round ten on inside bend

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
X is the Roman numeral for ten

indicators.note: inside asks for the inner letters of the word bend, dropping its ends

explanation.surface: Someone steers a vehicle round a bend in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steers' looks like a verb about driving, but it is the noun: young castrated bulls.
explanation.definitionFit: Steers are castrated male cattle, and oxen is the general plural for such beasts.

clue.text: Cooked bream's colour

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of the fish are worked into a new form

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A fish turns a particular shade once it is cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is a yellowish-orange colour, named after fossil resin.

clue.text: Wonderful not having short visit by wise men

indicators.note: not having means those letters are taken away from the longer word

parts.note: magical means wonderful or enchanting

indicators.note: short means the word for visit loses its final letter

parts.note: a call is a brief visit

explanation.surface: Something marvellous is spoiled because a quick visit from wise men never happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims CALL to CAL, and 'not having' takes CAL out of MAGICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi are the wise men from the East who visited the infant Jesus.

clue.text: Private lines from naughty mag of this kind

parts.note: a GI is a private soldier in the US Army
RLY is an abbreviation for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A soldier reads lines from a saucy magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: A girly magazine features photographs of scantily clad women.
explanation.definitionFit: A risque magazine of this type is called a girly mag.

clue.text: Leading surgeon maps out muscular contraction

indicators.note: leading picks the first letter of the word surgeon
out suggests the letters of maps are put out of order

explanation.surface: A top surgeon charts the course of a cramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A spasm is a sudden involuntary contraction of a muscle.

clue.text: Made divine whichever way you look at it

indicators.text: whichever way you look at it
indicators.note: this says the word reads identically forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone has been made a god, however you view the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whichever way you look at it' sounds like an idiom meaning 'in any case', but it says the answer is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: To deify is to make a god of someone, so deified means made divine.

clue.text: Well-liked turn in part of East London

indicators.note: in places the turn inside the district's name

parts.note: Poplar is a district of East London, in Tower Hamlets
a U-turn gives the letter U

explanation.surface: A favoured act performs in an East End venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular means liked by many people, a direct synonym of well-liked.

clue.text: Slur the corrupted conman

indicators.note: corrupted says the letters of the preceding words are spoiled into another order

explanation.surface: A swindler is accused of a corrupt slur.
explanation.definitionFit: A hustler is a swindler who cons people out of money.

clue.text: Idiot partly a wag

parts.note: half means partly, as in half-done
a wit is a witty person, a wag

explanation.surface: A fool is partly a joker.
explanation.definitionFit: A halfwit is a foolish or stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Regular course of action in being way out

indicators.note: out means the way word sits outside the short word

parts.note: a route is a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's normal behaviour is to be far out of the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A routine is a regular, habitual sequence of actions.

clue.text: Way one is using some milk outside to produce sauce

indicators.note: outside means the milk word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: curd is the thick part of milk, some of it separated out
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
A stands for one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A recipe uses some milk to make a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Custard is a sweet sauce made from milk and eggs, poured over puddings.

clue.text: Fielder may do this if he fails to do this!

definitions.text: Fielder may do this if he fails to do this!

parts.words: Fielder may do this if he fails to do this!
parts.note: a fielder who drops the ball will get a telling-off; one phrase means both taking the ball and being scolded

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a fielder tries to take the ball before it lands; dropping a catch gets you a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to take the ball and, idiomatically, to be told off or punished.

clue.text: Desperately determined to perform with gold cube

parts.note: to do is to perform
or is gold in heraldry
a die is a small cube used in games

explanation.surface: Someone is set on performing with a golden die.
explanation.definitionFit: A do-or-die effort is one made with desperate determination, risking everything.

clue.text: Delayed having most of the milky sap

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped from the sap word

parts.note: latex is the milky sap of rubber trees

explanation.surface: Something is held up because of sticky sap.
explanation.definitionFit: Late means delayed, coming after the expected time.

clue.text: Leave old capital

parts.note: to quit is to leave

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a former capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Quito is the capital city of Ecuador.

clue.text: Australian's startling exclamation at court order

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for Australian, and the possessive gives an S
bo, also spelt boo, is a cry made to startle someone

explanation.surface: An Australian cries out in shock at a ruling from the court.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO was a British Anti-Social Behaviour Order, a court order restricting someone's conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: An ASBO was a civil court order in the UK that restricted antisocial behaviour.

clue.text: Notice something opening

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
it stands for an unspecified thing

explanation.surface: Someone spots something with an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: An adit is a horizontal entrance or opening into a mine.

clue.text: Most of panel on a Scottish island

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the panel word is dropped

parts.note: a jury is a panel deciding a case

explanation.surface: Most of a committee is on an island in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Jura is an island in the Inner Hebrides, off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Forever said to have gone round and round with nurse about where in France?

indicators.note: said indicates that a word is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: whirled means spun round and round
taken as written
ou is French for where; about merely joins it to the nursing word
to tend is to nurse

explanation.surface: Someone spun dizzily with a nurse, wondering where in France they were.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase closes the Christian doxology ('Glory be...'); 'said' signals that a spun-around word is heard, and 'where in France' wants a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: The liturgical phrase from the Gloria means eternally, without ceasing, hence forever.

clue.text: In part, restless support given to board

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone is partly restless, needing support at a meeting of the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In part' looks like the hidden indicator, but 'part' supplies the opening T of the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a framework that supports a board to make a table.

clue.text: Tyre oddly having sufficient tread

indicators.note: oddly picks the first and third letters of the word tyre

parts.note: ample means sufficient or enough

explanation.surface: A car tyre has enough tread on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tread' looks like the noun on a tyre, but it is the verb: to tread on is to trample.
explanation.definitionFit: To trample is to tread heavily on something, crushing it underfoot.
